proposals.evidence: Platts p. 141 distinguishes Arabic-derived Urdu/Hindi badan “body” from Hindi badan “mouth/face” descended from vadana. Only the body sense is linked here. Provisional immediate-donor hypothesis: Hindi/Urdu, with borrowing between neighboring Indo-Aryan languages still possible. The source establishes the lexical family, not the direction of transfer into this particular survey locality. proposals.evidence: Platts p. 33 documents Urdu/Hindi ādmī “human being, man, husband”. The survey admi/adami/adimi family has the same consonants and documented man/husband senses, with vowel insertion or rounding. The exact earlier Arabic/Persian history is not represented by a direct remote-ancestor edge. Provisional immediate-donor hypothesis: Hindi/Urdu, with borrowing between neighboring Indo-Aryan languages still possible.
